pages.text: Kweku loved the school drum club. But he was the slowest learner in the club. When Madam Efe taught a new rhythm, the others got it in two tries. Kweku needed ten.
sentences: Kweku loved the school drum club.
But he was the slowest learner in the club.
When Madam Efe taught a new rhythm, the others got it in two tries.
Kweku needed ten.
pages.alt: A boy practises with a drum while other children play quickly behind him.

pages.text: The others did not tease him, but Kweku still felt small. ‘Maybe drums are not for me,’ he told his grandfather that evening.
sentences: The others did not tease him, but Kweku still felt small.
‘Maybe drums are not for me,’ he told his grandfather that evening.
pages.alt: The boy sits on a step with his drum in his lap, speaking to his grandfather.

pages.text: Grandfather smiled. ‘In any drum group,’ he said, ‘somebody keeps the slow, steady beat. Try to feel it in your heart, like a walking pace.’
sentences: Grandfather smiled.
‘In any drum group,’ he said, ‘somebody keeps the slow, steady beat.
Try to feel it in your heart, like a walking pace.’
pages.alt: An old man gently taps his chest as the boy listens.

pages.text: Every day on the way to school, Kweku tapped the beat on his knee. Tap… tap… tap… He did not rush. He listened to his feet.
sentences: Every day on the way to school, Kweku tapped the beat on his knee.
Tap… tap… tap… He did not rush.
He listened to his feet.
pages.alt: The boy walks along a path, tapping his knee in time with his steps.

pages.text: On the day of the school concert, the club began a fast, exciting rhythm. After a few bars, some drummers sped up and some slowed down. The music was falling apart!
sentences: On the day of the school concert, the club began a fast, exciting rhythm.
After a few bars, some drummers sped up and some slowed down.
The music was falling apart!
pages.alt: Seven children drum on a stage while their faces show worry.

pages.text: Kweku did not panic. He played his slow, steady beat, loud and clear. Boom… boom… boom… One by one, the others heard it and found their way back.
sentences: Kweku did not panic.
He played his slow, steady beat, loud and clear.
Boom… boom… boom… One by one, the others heard it and found their way back.
pages.alt: The boy drums boldly while the other children turn to watch him and join in.

pages.text: The audience clapped along with Kweku’s beat. When the music ended, Madam Efe said, ‘Kweku, you were the heartbeat of our group tonight.’
sentences: The audience clapped along with Kweku’s beat.
When the music ended, Madam Efe said, ‘Kweku, you were the heartbeat of our group tonight.’
pages.alt: A crowd claps as the teacher gives the boy a proud look.

pages.text: Kweku grinned. He was still not the fastest learner. But he had discovered that every person in a team has something special to give. The end.
sentences: Kweku grinned.

pages.alt: The boy smiles with his drum, surrounded by the other children.
